rows.note: CME first seen to the NE in STEREO A COR2 starting at 2026-10-07T13:53Z. So far it is only visible in COR2A. The source of this CME is a C7.9 class flare from AR 14549 (N10W04) peaking at 2026-10-07T13:17Z best seen in SDO AIA 171. Some dimming and an EUVI wave associated with the eruption can be seen in SDO AIA 193. Some deflection is evident in the measurement of this CME, likely due to it close proximity to a coronal hole to the SE of AR 14549.

cmeAnalyses.note: Measurement based on best fit among SOHO LASCO C2/C3, GOES CCOR-1, and STEREO A COR2.

rows.note: CME faintly seen to the east in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and GOES CCOR-1. The CME may potentially be visible to the west in STEREO A COR2. The potential source for this CME may be beyond the east limb, as moving field lines are seen in SDO AIA 193 starting around 2026-10-08T09:21Z. Some ejecta of material can also be seen beyond the east limb in GOES SUVI 304 as well.

cmeAnalyses.note: Measurement based on the best fit between SOHO LASCO C3, GOES CCOR-1, and STEREO A COR2 imagery in SWPC_CAT. Due to the CME's faintness, this CME measurement is more approximate than usual.

rows.note: CME visible to the west in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and GOES CCOR-1 as well as possibly faintly to the east in STEREO A COR2. This CME overlaps in the field of view with the CME first seen in STEREO A COR2 at 2026-10-08T16:53Z. The potential source is a filament eruption centered around N05W25 as best seen in SDO AIA 193/304 imagery. The eruption is best seen as dimming starting at 2026-10-08T09:21Z in SDO AIA 193. The filament liftoff can be best seen from the point of view of STEREO A EUV 195/304, in the NE quadrant from the point of view of STEREO A.

cmeAnalyses.note: Measurement based on potential source location as well as best fit between SOHO LASCO C3, GOES CCOR-1, and STEREO A COR2. There were two measurable frames of STEREO A COR2 imagery available for this measurement. There may be some deflection of the CME.

rows.note: CME visible to the NE in STEREO A COR2 and the NW in GOES CCOR-1. There was a real-time data gap in SOHO LASCO imagery at the start of the CME, but this backfilled with additional imagery. The source for this CME is an M6.7 class flare from AR 14549 (N12W20) which peaked at 2026-10-08T15:48Z. The flare is best seen in SDO AIA 131. The accompanying EUV wave which spans the entire NW quadrant of the Earth-facing disk is best seen in SDO AIA 193. The eruption is also visible in STEREO A EUV 195/304 imagery.

cmeAnalyses.note: Preliminary measurement of the leading edge based on the best fit between GOES CCOR-1 and STEREO A COR2 imagery in SWPC_CAT.
Preliminary shock measurement using the best fit between GOES CCOR-1 and STEREO A COR2 imagery in SWPC_CAT.
Updated measurement of the leading edge of the CME based on the source location as well as the best fit between SOHO LASCO C3, GOES CCOR-1, and STEREO A COR2 imagery.

rows.note: Faint CME observed to the E only in STEREO A COR2 Science Data, as a real-time gap in STEREO A COR2 beacon data spanning 2026-10-08T18:53Z to 2026-10-09T17:53Z obscured real-time observations of this CME. CME leading edge not observed in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 or GOES CCOR-1. Partial overlap with CMEs 2026-10-08T16:24Z and CME 2026-10-08T16:53Z. The source is an on-disk filament eruption in the vicinity of AR 14548, starting around 2026-10-08T17:13Z, with the filament spanning a curved arc from S08E15 to S21E24 to S15E05 before liftoff in SDO AIA 304. Eruption observed as filament ejecta, brightening, and double-ribbon flare in SDO AIA 304, and as field line movement, dimming, and brightening/post-eruptive arcades in SDO AIA 171/193/211.

cmeAnalyses.note: 3D STEREO A COR2 Science Data only analysis, fitting to the approximate center of the eruptive source ~S16E13 and finding northward deflection. Science data imagery is used due to a real-time STEREO A COR2 beacon data gap spanning 2026-10-08T18:53Z to 2026-10-09T17:53Z, and no leading edge observations in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and GOES CCOR-1.

rows.note: CME visible to the NW in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and GOES CCOR-1, directly following CME: 2026-10-08T16:53Z in the field of view. The CME is not visible in STEREO A COR2, and a data gap starts at 2026-10-08T18:53Z. The potential source is unclear, with several potential source candidates on the disk. The most likely candidate is a possible eruption from AR 14547 (N15W85) seen starting around 2026-10-08T16:19Z as dimming and moving field lines. The eruption is also faintly visible from the point of view of STEREO A EUV 195 imagery. Another candidate source is a filament eruption starting around 2026-10-08T18:09Z centered around S15E10 as seen in SDO AIA 193/304, but this is not a likely source candidate due to the location of the eruption. This eruption's proximity to a coronal hole may result in some deflection of the eruption. The third possible eruption candidate is activity from AR 14549 (N10W25), but it is not clear if this is a separate eruption from the one that produced CME: 2026-10-08T16:53Z.

cmeAnalyses.note: Measurement based on the potential source location. STEREO A COR2 was not available for triangulation of this measurement.

rows.note: CME faintly seen to the east in GOES CCOR-1 imagery. There is a data gap in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 imagery starting at 2026-10-09T00:48Z and a data gap starting in STEREO A COR2 at 2026-10-09T00:53Z. The source is likely beyond the E limb as seen in available EUV imagery, as slow moving field lines are visible on the E limb in SDO AIA 193 and GOES SUVI 284 imagery starting as early as 2026-10-08T18:30Z.

cmeAnalyses.note: Plane of sky measurement using GOES CCOR-1 running difference imagery in SWPC_CAT.

rows.note: CME seen to the NW in GOES CCOR-1 imagery. There is a data gap in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and STEREO A COR2 at the time of this CME. The potential source is unclear, but is likely an eruption from AR 14547 (approximately N15W90) starting around 2026-10-09T06:30Z, best seen as moving/opening field lines in SDO AIA 193 and GOES SUVI 284 imagery.

cmeAnalyses.note: Measurement based on source location using GOES CCOR-1 imagery.

rows.note: CME visible to the NNW in GOES CCOR-1 imagery. There is no SOHO LASCO C2/C3 or STEREO A COR2 data available during this time, with a data gap in SOHO imagery starting at 2026-10-09T00:48Z and no STEREO A COR2 data available since 2026-10-09T01:09Z. The source for this CME is not found in available EUV imagery.

cmeAnalyses.note: Plane of sky measurement using GOES CCOR-1 running difference imagery in SWPC_CAT.

rows.note: Faint CME with a loop front seen to the NW in the early SOHO LASCO C2 imagery, also seen faintly in C3 and GOES CCOR-1. It is fully covered by long data gap in STEREO A COR2 coronagraph. The source is the occulted (or on-limb) M1.3 flare likely from Active Region 14547 (N15W94), now decayed to a plage, which had just rotated off the visible disk before the flare. Other coronal signatures include a small ejecta seen in SDO AIA 304 at the time of the flare and movement/opening of field lines seen to the NW behind the limb in SDO AIA 171/193 and GOES SUVI 304/284.

cmeAnalyses.note: Analysis based on the location of the source (the M1.3 flare from Active Region 14547 (N15W94) which had just rotated off the visible disk before the flare) and on imagery from SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and GOES CCOR-1 The CME is fully covered by long data gap in STEREO A COR2 coronagraph, so this analysis is not confirmed by STEREO A.

rows.note: CME observed to the NW in SOHO LASCO C2/C3, GOES CCOR-1, and STEREO A COR2. The source is former AR 14547 (~N15W105) as directly observed by STEREO A around the west limb from SDO. Observed across SDO AIA 131/171/193/211/304 as field line movement and EUV wave, and brightening, starting around 2026-10-10T07:51Z, partially obscured by a rare transit of the moon across the SDO AIA field-of-view. Also seen in STEREO A EUVI 195/304 as brightening, dimming, and field line movement starting around 2026-10-10T07:55Z.

cmeAnalyses.note: Triangulation between SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and STEREO A COR2.

rows.note: Very minor faint and narrow CME seen to the NE in STEREO A COR2 coronagraph in early timestamps. This is Possibly the same faint narrow CME that is also seen at the time NE in SOHO LASCO C2 for a few early timestamps and not seen in C3 or GOES C3. No source has been found  in EUV imagery for this event.

cmeAnalyses.note: Analysis based on the fit of the narrow NE fronts in STEREO A COR2 and SOHO LASCO C2.

rows.note: CME observed to the NW in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and GOES CCOR-1, with a full halo shock. Not yet observed in STEREO A COR2 white light imagery. The source is AR 14549, associated with an M6.4 flare peaking at 2026-10-10T15:10Z observed in SDO AIA 131. Also observed starting around 2026-10-10T15:04Z as field line movement and very large EUV wave, some dimming, and brightening/post eruptive arcade in SDO AIA 131/171/193/211/304.

cmeAnalyses.note: Preliminary bulk. SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and GOES CCOR-1 fit using W54 as the flare longitude, given no available STEREO A COR2 to triangulate with.

SHOCK preliminary analysis, somewhat speculative using SOHO LASCO C2/C3 only (CCOR-1 observes, but does not track perfectly between LASCO/CCOR-1), with no usable STEREO A COR2 imagery available to triangulate. This analyzed longitude is significantly far from the eruptive source around W54 degrees, but the entire shock front does not otherwise fit within the swpc_cat tool at more western longitudes.

rows.note: Minor faint, narrow CME/outflow seen to the west in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and GOES CCOR-1 and covered by the data gap in STEREO A. No clear source has been found for this CME.

cmeAnalyses.note: This minor CME is not seen in STEREO A COR2 because of the data gap in STEREO. No source has been found for this CME. Only plane-of-sky analysis is possible for this CME.

rows.note: Outflow first seen to the NW in SOHO LASCO C2 starting around 2026-10-11T09:12Z. This feature is much easier to see later in its propagation into SOHO LASCO C3, GOES CCOR-1, and STEREO A COR2. The source is most likely outflow following CME: 2026-10-10T16:15Z but may be related to field line movement seen near the NW limb in SDO AIA 193 starting as early as 2026-10-11T05:00Z.

cmeAnalyses.note: Measurement based on best fit among SOHO LASCO C2/C3, GOES CCOR-1, and STEREO A COR2.

rows.note: This CME is visible to the east in GOES CCOR-1 and SOHO LASCO C2/C3 imagery. This event is seen in STEREO A COR2, directed towards the east, after it has exceeded the field of view due to a data gap from 2026-10-11T17:38Z to 2026-10-12T01:53Z. The source is a filament eruption spanning S30E30 to S10E05 which begins to lift off around 2026-10-11T22:30Z as seen in SDO 131/171/193/304 and GOES SUVI 131/171/195/284/304 imagery. Dimming is visible in SDO AIA 193 and GOES SUVI 195 imagery, with post eruptive arcades visible starting around 2026-10-11T23:40Z.

cmeAnalyses.note: Measurement based on the approximate source location. Although this leading edge for this event is outside of the STEREO A COR2 field of view, this imagery was used as a guide to find the best fitting parameters between SOHO LASCO C3 and STEREO A COR2 imagery.

rows.note: This CME is visible to the southwest in GOES CCOR-1 and SOHO LASCO C2/C3 imagery. This event is not seen in STEREO A COR2 in real-time due to a data gap starting at 2026-10-11T17:38Z. The source may be related to dimming centered near S20E30 starting around 2026-10-11T22:00Z as seen in SDO AIA 193 and GOES SUVI 195 imagery.

cmeAnalyses.note: Measured longitude based on the source location. Due to a data gap in STEREO A COR2 imagery, a triangulated measurement was not available and the measured parameters may vary slightly as a result.

rows.note: This CME is visible to the east in SOHO LASCO C2/C3, GOES CCOR-1, and STEREO A COR2 imagery. Dimming is visible in SDO AIA 193 and GOES SUVI 195 imagery, with post eruptive arcades visible starting around 2026-10-12T05:45Z.

cmeAnalyses.note: Measurement based on the approximate source location and best fit between SOHO LASCO C3 and STEREO A COR2 imagery.

rows.note: This CME is visible to the west in STEREO A COR2, SOHO LASCO C2/C3, and GOES CCOR-1 imagery. The source is likely related to a filament eruption visible beyond the western limb in STEREO A EUVI 195/304 imagery which lifts-off around 2026-10-12T10:15Z.

cmeAnalyses.note: Measurement based on the best fit between SOHO LASCO C3 and STEREO A COR2 imagery.

The source of this event is rising field line loops seen originating from beyond the SW limb in SDO AIA 171 beginning at approx. 2026-10-12T18:18Z.

cmeAnalyses.note: Plane-of-sky using a longitude of W90 due to source from beyond the SW limb and lack of available STEREO A COR2 imagery to triangulate.

rows.note: Bright CME first seen to the NE by SOHO LASCO C2 beginning at 2026-10-14T13:36Z, as well as by SOHO LASCO C3, STEREO A COR2 and GOES CCOR-1 in later frames. The source of this event is a filament eruption centered at approx. N45E20 seen beginning at approx. 2026-10-14T10:05Z in SDO AIA, GOES SUVI and STEREO A EUVI 304 imagery. Dimming and field line opening can also be seen in SDO AIA 171/193, GOES SUVI 284 and STEREO A EUVI 195 imagery.

cmeAnalyses.note: Measurement based on approximate source location and best fit in SOHO LASCO C2/C3, STEREO A COR2 and GOES CCOR-1.

The source of this CME may be related to an unstable filament seen along the West limb in STEREO A EUVI 304 imagery beginning at approx. 2026-10-14T18:45Z.

cmeAnalyses.note: STEREO A plane-of-sky using a longitude of W160 due to source on or beyond the STEREO A West limb and no available SOHO LASCO or GOES CCOR imagery to triangulate.

rows.note: CME first seen to the NE by SOHO LASCO C2 beginning at 2026-10-14T23:12Z. Field line opening is also seen in GOES SUVI 284 in association with this eruption.

cmeAnalyses.note: Measurement based on approximate source location and best fit in SOHO LASCO C2/C3, STEREO A COR2 and GOES CCOR-1.

cmeAnalyses.note: Plane of sky measurement using SOHO LASCO C2/C3 running difference imagery in SWPC_CAT.

rows.note: Faint, wide CME visible to the SW in STEREO A COR2 only. The CME is not clearly seen in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 or GOES CCOR-1 imagery. The potential source is not clearly visible. There is a data gap in STEREO A COR2 and EUV imagery in real-time from 2026-10-15T12:09Z to 2026-10-16T06:09Z. A potential source may be seen in STEREO A EUV imagery anywhere from longitudes W90 to approximately W120 as a gradual, minor dimming may be seen after the data gap starting around 2026-10-16T06:09Z. However, there are not strong post-eruption signatures in imagery, and there is low confidence in this analysis of the source location.

cmeAnalyses.note: Plane of sky measurement using STEREO A COR2 running difference imagery in SWPC_CAT.

rows.note: Narrow CME visible to the SW in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and GOES CCOR-1 imagery. The CME is not visible in STEREO A COR2 imagery. No source is found for this CME in EUV imagery.

cmeAnalyses.note: Plane of sky measurement using GOES CCOR-1 imagery in SWPC_CAT.

cmeAnalyses.note: Plane of sky measurement using GOES CCOR-1 running difference imagery in SWPC_CAT.

rows.note: CME visible faintly to the NE in STEREO A COR2. The CME is not seen in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 or GOES CCOR-1 imagery. The potential source is an eruption starting around 2026-10-16T11:00Z, primarily centered around N05E10, although the eruption extends as far east as N05E30. The eruption may include a filament liftoff as seen in SDO AIA 304. Dimming, moving/opening field lines, and post-eruptive arcades are best seen in SDO AIA 193. The eruption is also seen near the NE limb from the point of view of STEREO A EUV 195 and 304 imagery. This CME may exhibit deflection due to its proximity to the coronal hole.

cmeAnalyses.note: Measurement using limited available frames of STEREO A COR2 imagery before the leading edge of the CME becomes too faint to measure. The measurement is based on the approximate source location and is approximate due to the possible deflection of the eruption and the eruption's longitudinal extent.

rows.note: Bright CME seen to the NW in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and to the NW in STEREO A COR2. Its source is likely a messy eruption seen in the NW quadrant in STEREO A EUV 195/304 and centered very approximately around N12W140 near former Active Region 14549 starting 2026-10-16T14:25Z. Coronal signatures include dimming, post-eruptive arcades and ejecta seen in STEREO A EUV 195/304, as well as opening/moving of field lines behind the NW limb in SDO AIA 193/171.

cmeAnalyses.note: Analysis based on the fit of the clear front in two coronagraphs (SOHO LASCO and STEREO A COR2) and confirmed by the somewhat approximate location of the source in EUV imagery.

rows.note: Faint and narrow CME seen to the E in early SOHO LASCO C2 imagery and not seen in C3, GOES CCOR-1 and STEREO A COR2 imagery, likely because of its faintness. The start time is likely at least an hour earlier but the CME becomes clear around 17Z. No clear source found, so the CME is likely far sided.

cmeAnalyses.note: The CME is only seen in the early SOHO LASCO C2 imagery and its source has not been found, so only plane-of-sky analysis is possible.

cmeAnalyses.note: The CME is not seen in STEREO A COR2 coronagraph and no source has been found for this CME in EUV imagery, so only plane-of-sky analysis is possible.

rows.note: CME first seen to the ESE in SOHO LASCO C2 starting at 2026-10-17T02:48Z. It is also seen to the E in SOHO LASCO C3. The CME is also seen later in its propagation to the E GOES CCOR-1 near the edge of the  FOV as the early frames of the CME are obscured by Earthshine. It is also seen to the SE in STEREO A COR2 as a partial halo. The leading edge of the CME is somewhat irregularly shared with the nose farther to the south. The source is a filament eruption on or slightly beyond the SE limb best seen in SDO AIA 304 beginning around 2026-10-17T01:00Z. A wide opening of field lines can also been seen in SDO AIA 171 and SDO AIA 193.

cmeAnalyses.note: Measurement based on best fit among SOHO LASCO C2/C3, GOES CCOR-1, and STEREO A COR2.

cmeAnalyses.note: The CME is not seen in STEREO A COR2 coronagraph and its source has not been found (possibly far-sided), so only plane-of-sky analysis is possible.

cmeAnalyses.note: Measurement based on approximate source location and best fit in GOES CCOR-1.

The source of this CME is an eruption beyond the NW limb seen as moving field lines beyond the NW limb in STEREO A EUVI 195 beginning around 2026-10-19T11:05Z. The eruption likely occurred in proximity to a large coronal hole that is approaching the western limb from the perspective of STEREO A. Some deflection is likely.

cmeAnalyses.note: Measurement based on best fit among SOHO LASCO C2/C3, GOES CCOR-1, and STEREO A COR2.

The source is likely far-sided from Earth, observed around N10W130 as brightening in STEREO A EUVI 304 at 2026-10-19T18:15Z, and EUVI 195 at 2026-10-19T18:25Z. The source of this CME is most likely far-sided due to a lack of source candidates on the Earth-facing disk. Some very faint field line movement beyond the N limb in GOES SUVI 284 that may be related is visible beginning around 2026-10-19T23:00Z. A far-sided source is consistent with triangulated measurements.

cmeAnalyses.note: Measurement based on best fit among SOHO LASCO C2/C3, GOES CCOR-1, and STEREO A COR2.

cmeAnalyses.note: Measurement based on best fit between SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and STEREO A COR2.

cmeAnalyses.note: Measurement based on best fit among SOHO LASCO C2/C3, GOES CCOR-1, and STEREO A COR2.

rows.note: CME first seen to the East by STEREO A COR2 beginning at 2026-10-21T08:53Z, as well as by SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and GOES CCOR-1 in later frames. The source of this event is a small eruption seen centered at approx. N40E05 beginning at approx. 2026-10-21T08:15Z as seen in SDO AIA 193. Dimming signatures extending to the Southeast (approx. N20E25) seen in SDO AIA 193 and proximity to a small coronal hole indicate a potential strong SE deflection of this event.

cmeAnalyses.note: Measurement based on approximate source location and best fit in SOHO LASCO C2/C3, STEREO A COR2 and GOES CCOR-1.
